turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, and my son learned he got a zero from his phone in the middle of a class, before anyone picked up a phone to call me. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Thank you for coming in, Meredith. Please sit. I know this is not how you wanted to spend your afternoon, and I am grateful you made the time.
I'm not here to be thanked, Hale. I'm standing because I have twenty minutes. Owen found out about the zero on his phone. Did you call me before you entered it?
Before anything else: you are right that I should have called you before the zero went in. I did not, Owen saw it on his phone, and I am genuinely sorry. That one is mine.
Okay. Now the basis. What did you have on the day you entered it, apart from the software?
Take your time. I would like to hear what you are most worried about, before I say anything about the essay.

I'm worried about the zero, and I'm worried about the three weeks before Owen's Prestige deadline. I'm not going to talk about what worries me before you show me what you've got. Which document are you holding?
That makes complete sense. You must be a wonderful mother and a wonderful advocate. Owen is lucky to have you.
Don't manage me, Hale. Which document?
I mean it. I teach a lot of kids and I can tell when one has a parent in their corner.
Then you'll understand I'm not going to let a compliment change the subject. What do you have on the essay itself, apart from the checker's score?
Of course. I have the version history open on my laptop. I'll tell you what I see rather than rush you. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with a title only.
"Created at 11:31 PM Wednesday, title only." Okay. Turn the screen so I can see it. And what's the next timestamp?
At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more in another single edit. After that there are 23 minutes of small edits, font, his name, spacing. No earlier drafts exist.
"Two pastes, 612 and 794 words, and then formatting for twenty-three minutes." I'm writing those times down. What about the drafts before Wednesday night? Are there any?
I know that is hard to hear, and I do not claim it proves anything alone. Would you like to look at the screen yourself? Take as long as you need.
Show me. Turn the screen.

Thank you for your patience. The second thing is a quotation in his second body paragraph: Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' I have searched the full text and that line is not in the play.
"Not in the play." Okay. Did Owen's essay give a source for that line, or is it just in the text?
I would like to be fair to Owen. Is there any ordinary way a student could end up with an invented quotation in his own essay, in your view?

That's a question about Owen, and I won't answer hypotheticals about my son. You have a fake quote and a paste, and you have twenty minutes of my time. Is Owen allowed to be heard before any mark stands? Yes or no, Hale.
Yes. Absolutely. Owen should be heard before any mark stands, and I got that order wrong. I would like him to have that chance.

Okay. Then here's what I want, in writing, today: the zero withdrawn, Owen's mark held open, and a supervised rewrite, done privately, not in front of his class. Nothing goes on his record. Put it in an email yourself, and I'll want it by tomorrow at four.
Meredith, I want to say something I should have said at the start. I do not know what happened. I have concerns, and I have evidence, but I am not certain, and I may be wrong.

"Not certain." Okay. Then the rewrite is the fair way to find out, and the zero comes off the gradebook while we do it. Nothing on his record, and nothing in front of his class. I want that in an email from you before I leave this room.
The screen is turned toward you now. Take a moment. I'm in no hurry.

I've seen it. Two pastes, 612 and 794 words, and nothing before Wednesday night. That's your evidence, and it's more than the checker's score. It still doesn't say Owen didn't write it, so I'm holding my position. The rewrite is supervised, private, and the zero comes off the gradebook while it happens. Put that in an email by tomorrow at four, cc the principal, and nothing goes on his record.
Is there anything about this you would like me to explain better? I would rather you leave understanding my reasoning, even if you disagree with my conclusion.

I understand your reasoning, Hale. I don't need it explained again. Your terms are an email by tomorrow at four, the zero off the gradebook, a private supervised rewrite, and nothing on his record. Put them in writing.
You've been remarkably fair with me today, and I appreciate it.
Don't thank me yet. I haven't seen that email.
Can I ask how Owen has been since Tuesday? I've been worried about him too.
"Worried about him too." That's not what this meeting is about, Hale. Owen's been humiliated in front of his class, and you're asking me how he's doing. Put the terms in writing by tomorrow at four.
